patterns.label: Lexical Form
patterns.explain: The preposition takes its lexical form (לְ, בְּ, כְּ) before a consonant that has a full vowel, unless that syllable is the tone syllable.

patterns.label: Simple Sheva
patterns.explain: Before a consonant with a simple vocal sheva, the preposition takes a ḥireq (לִ, בִּ, כִּ).

patterns.label: Compound Sheva
patterns.explain: Before a compound sheva (a ḥāṭef), the preposition takes the short vowel that matches the ḥāṭef: pataḥ before a ḥāṭef-pataḥ (לַ), segol before a ḥāṭef-segol (לֶ), and qameṣ-ḥaṭuf before a ḥāṭef-qāmeṣ (לָ).

patterns.label: יְ
patterns.explain: Before a noun that begins with יְ, the preposition takes a ḥireq and the yod loses its sheva (לִי, בִּי, כִּי).

patterns.label: Tone Syllable
patterns.explain: Before a tone syllable, or before a monosyllabic word, the preposition takes a qameṣ (לָ, בָּ, כָּ).

patterns.label: Definite Article
patterns.explain: The definite article is prefixed: its ה drops out, but the preposition takes the vowel the article would have. Before א, ר or ע the article lengthens its vowel to make up for the rejected dagesh (compensatory lengthening), so the preposition takes a qameṣ (לָ, בָּ, כָּ).

patterns.label: Definite Article
patterns.explain: The definite article is prefixed: its ה drops out, but the preposition takes the vowel the article would have. With the article’s lexical form, the preposition takes pataḥ (לַ, בַּ, כַּ) and the noun’s first letter has a dagesh forte.

patterns.label: Definite Article
patterns.explain: The definite article is prefixed: its ה drops out, but the preposition takes the vowel the article would have. With implicit doubling before ה, ח or ע, the preposition takes pataḥ (לַ, בַּ, כַּ) and no dagesh is written.

patterns.label: Definite Article
patterns.explain: The definite article is prefixed: its ה drops out, but the preposition takes the vowel the article would have. Before an unaccented ה or ע with a qameṣ, the article would be הֶ, so the preposition takes segol (לֶ, בֶּ, כֶּ).

patterns.label: יהוה
patterns.explain: Before the divine name יהוה, the preposition takes pataḥ (לַ, בַּ, כַּ).

patterns.label: אֱ
patterns.explain: Sometimes, before אֱ, the preposition takes ṣere (לֵ, בֵּ, כֵּ).

table.rule: Before a consonant that has a full vowel, except before a tone syllable.
Before a consonant that has a simple vocal sheva.
Before a compound sheva (ֲ ֱ ֳ). The preposition takes the short vowel that matches the ḥāṭef: pataḥ, segol or qameṣ-ḥaṭuf.
Before a noun that begins with יְ. The yod loses its sheva.
Before a tone syllable, or before a monosyllabic word.
Compensatory lengthening, because of the prefixed definite article.
Before some words that have the definite article: the article’s lexical form or implicit doubling.
